advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Document recreating BOTH markers (.gate-scratch-required on root AND .gate-scratch-mounted on the volume) in review-bot-ops.md recovery, matching provision-restore.md's 'the markers'.
evidence: review-bot-ops.md recovery block only touches the proof: 'recreate it — it is a marker, not data: `touch /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch/.gate-scratch-mounted`.'
provision-restore.md:133 'If the markers are missing, `touch` them (see `review-bot-ops.md`)' — but review-bot-ops.md documents recreating only ONE of the two markers.
gate_admission.py:171-172 — a missing .gate-scratch-required makes _require_scratch_volume return silently, so a lost declaration disarms the guard (admits) rather than refusing.
advisory.finding: The restore recovery guidance only recreates the PROOF marker (.gate-scratch-mounted), never the DECLARATION marker (.gate-scratch-required). provision-restore.md step 4b says 'If the markers are missing, `touch` them (see `review-bot-ops.md`)', but review-bot-ops.md's 'volume is not mounted' recovery documents only `touch /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch/.gate-scratch-mounted`. On a restore that reuses an instance whose root filesystem was rebuilt (declaration lost) but the volume is genuinely unmounted, following the runbook leaves the declaration absent, so _require_scratch_volume() returns silently (declaration-absent = today's behaviour) and gates run on the ROOT filesystem — the exact silent fallback the epic exists to prevent, with no doc step to restore the declaration.
scenarios: Restore onto a fresh/rebuilt root FS where the volume did not remount but the declaration marker was lost; operator follows the runbook, touches only the proof marker, gates silently run on root.
advisory.suggested_fix: In review-bot-ops.md's 'volume is not mounted' recovery, add `touch /var/lib/rebar/.gate-scratch-required` alongside the proof-marker touch, and note that the declaration on root is what arms the guard.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard the scratch `df` in observability.sh §2e so used-percent is only published when the volume is actually mounted (e.g. gate on the .gate-scratch-mounted proof marker), so the disk-high alarm never evaluates root's usage under the scratch mount dimension.
evidence: `df` on an unmounted mount-point path reports the stats of the underlying (root) filesystem, not the intended volume
The disk metric is dimensioned `mount=/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch` (line 189) so the disk-high alarm cannot tell it is reading root rather than the scratch volume
advisory.finding: observability.sh §2e computes the gate-scratch `disk_used_percent` via `df --output=pcent "$GATE_SCRATCH_MOUNT"`; when the volume is NOT mounted, `df` resolves to the containing ROOT filesystem and publishes root's usage under `mount=/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch`, so the `rebar-gate-scratch-disk-high` alarm evaluates a misleading value (root's %) precisely in the unmounted state.
scenarios: Scratch volume fails to mount at boot: gate_scratch_unmounted alarms correctly, but disk_used_percent{mount=gate-scratch} shows root's %, potentially masking or mis-reporting scratch pressure once remounted-and-filling
advisory.suggested_fix: Only run the `df`/put-metric-data block for the scratch mount when `[ "$scratch_mounted" -eq 1 ]`, so `disk_used_percent{mount=gate-scratch}` is absent (not root's value) while unmounted.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Bind the gate-scratch parent read-only where the container does not need to write it, or otherwise protect the .gate-scratch-required declaration marker from container-side deletion, so the refusal guard cannot be silently disarmed.
evidence: gate_admission._require_scratch_volume returns (admits) when `.gate-scratch-required` is absent: src/rebar/llm/gate_admission.py:171 `if not (base.parent / _SCRATCH_REQUIRED_MARKER).is_file(): return`
docker-compose comment notes the review-bot image runs as root (line ~281 'The review-bot image runs as root, so the root-owned host dir is writable')
advisory.finding: The review-bot container binds the mount's PARENT `/var/lib/rebar:/var/lib/rebar`, which is root-resident and carries the `.gate-scratch-required` declaration marker; the container runs as root, so a compromised or buggy container process can delete that root-side marker and silently disarm the refusal guard (declaration-absent => admits, falling back to root).
scenarios: A container-side process (or misbehaving cleanup) removes /var/lib/rebar/.gate-scratch-required; the next gate then admits on an unmounted volume and repopulates the store on root — the silent-revert the epic exists to prevent

advisory.finding: test_the_probe_reads_the_same_marker_the_gate_refusal_reads asserts on the TEXT of the script under test (observability.sh) rather than its behavior: it strips comments and checks `ga._SCRATCH_MOUNTED_MARKER in code` and `"mountpoint" not in code`. This is source-grepping the code under test; the second assertion in particular forbids an implementation substring with no observable consequence, so it would break on a behavior-preserving refactor (e.g. deciding mountedness via a helper, or reading the marker while additionally validating with mountpoint) even though the mounted/unmounted heartbeat behavior is already covered by test_a_mounted_scratch_volume... and test_an_unmounted_scratch_volume....
